$comment: Single source of truth for presets. Read by TypeScript and by
tools/generate_precomputed.py, so a preset cannot be defined in the app in
THREE MATCHED DATE PAIRS, solved by card.calibrate.solve_flood_rate:
2. Flood onset + 1 yr   <->  the selected post-Flood contact, K/Pg or N/Q.
3. End of the Ice Age   <->  a conventional Ice Age endpoint.
Three pairs need three unknowns, and the model now has them: lambda_F, the
in-Flood relaxation k_F, and the post-Flood relaxation k_PF. lambda is no
longer flat across the Flood year -- it starts at lambda_F, relaxes at k_F,
and hands the post-Flood exponential whatever it has reached at t_F2. That
handover is continuous, so k_F is one new degree of freedom rather than two.
This is what a single k could not do. Pinning only the Flood year's two ends
forced k * 1 yr = ln(pre/post), so the relaxation was spent within a decade
and the Cenozoic collapsed. With k_F and k_PF separate, the Flood year and
the millennia after it each get their own rate.
Naming rule: a value ending in _age is an AGE (years before present), one
ending in _date is a DATE (years after Day 1 of Creation).

flood_start.label: Precambrian-Cambrian
flood_start.note: Pre-Flood contact, matched to the Flood's onset.

ice_age_end.label: End of the Ice Age
ice_age_end.note: Conventional Ice Age endpoint, matched to the chronology's Ice Age date. 12 ka is the author's figure; the package's own run config ships 11.5 kyr.

masoretic.label: Masoretic
note: The package default (card.chronology.DEFAULT_CHRONOLOGY). ice_age_end_date
is a DATE -- years after Creation -- so the Ice Age ends at 2556 BP. The
Ice Age is not a calibration anchor in this structure; it is reported as a
prediction.

septuagint.label: Septuagint (LXX)
note: PROVISIONAL. Flood at 5324 BP is the author's figure; age_of_earth is still
a placeholder. Needs Rick's confirmation.
Note his geologic-column figure implies a Flood at ~5054 BP, which matches
neither chronology here exactly and is closest to this one.

flood_only.label: Flood only
note: No Creation-week acceleration; an instantaneous onset at t_F relaxing
as a single exponential. t_F == t_F2.

general.label: Creation week + Flood
note: Authored but not exposed in v1. Turning this on is flipping `enabled`;
no component changes, because the parameter panel iterates the free
names Python returns rather than a hardcoded list.
Freeing lambda_c/k_c does not disturb the calibration: both constraint
ages map to formation DATEs at or after t_F, so their integrals cover
only the Flood and post-Flood regions and the Creation-week parameters
never enter. Verified to exactly zero difference.
Grid for the precomputed first-paint layer. Log-spaced in true age: the
structure is all in the recent end. Breakpoints, constraint ages and the
relaxation regions are unioned in by the generator.

$flood_duration_note: True years between pairs 1 and 2 -- the Flood year. The chronology must give the Flood this length (flood_end_date = flood_start_date + this), because solve_flood_rate treats it as an input, never an unknown.

pt.label: Permian-Triassic (P-T)
pt.note: Post-Flood contact at 251.902 Ma (ICS; matches the Triassic base in data/ics-units.json).

kpg.label: Cretaceous-Paleogene (K/Pg)
kpg.note: Post-Flood contact at 66.0 Ma (ICS), one year after onset.

pe.label: Paleocene-Eocene (P-E)
pe.note: Post-Flood contact at 56.0 Ma (ICS; matches the Eocene base in data/ics-units.json).

eo.label: Eocene-Oligocene (E-O)
eo.note: Post-Flood contact at 33.9 Ma (ICS; matches the Oligocene base in data/ics-units.json).

om.label: Oligocene-Miocene (O-M)
om.note: Post-Flood contact at 23.03 Ma (ICS; matches the Miocene base in data/ics-units.json).

mp.label: Miocene-Pliocene (M-P)
mp.note: Post-Flood contact at 5.333 Ma (ICS; matches the Pliocene base in data/ics-units.json).

nq.label: Neogene-Quaternary (N/Q)
nq.note: Post-Flood contact at 2.58 Ma (ICS), one year after onset.

$note: How long after the Flood's end the Ice Age ended, in true years.
The third matched pair fixes k_PF, the post-Flood relaxation, so moving
this date moves the whole post-Flood curve. Expressed as an offset from
the Flood's end rather than as a DATE, because that is the quantity a
reader is actually reasoning about and it means the same thing in every
`default` is each chronology's own ice_age_end_date, kept so the shipped
calibration is unchanged: 1843 yr for Masoretic, 1123 for Septuagint.
Both are well outside the listed offsets, which is worth knowing before
